replies.author: @Rhymosophy
replies.text: I'm from Shetland. Funnily enough, the native Shetland pronunciation of 'Shetland' does sound like 'Shitland' to outsiders, and I've even seen some locals spelling it like that. However, it's actually Shaetlan(d) (the 'd' often isn't pronounced) - the 'ae' is a sound that doesn't occur in either English or Scots, and Shetlanders don't pronounce it the same as they do 'i'. In a Shetland accent, the first syllable in Shaet-lan doesn't rhyme with words like 'hit' and bit', it rhymes with words like 'paet' (peat) and 'baet' (beat), most of which are spelt with EA in English. (And in any case, in Shetland as in Scotland and parts of England, 'shit' is pronounced 'shite'!) The perception of it as an 'i' sound is owing to its resemblance to the 'i' sound in standard Scottish English, whereas in Shetland, the 'i' sound before 't' is pronounced more like the E in 'the'. What most Shetlanders really object to is the plural form 'Shetlands' rather than 'Shetland' although I personally think this is a bit of a storm in a teacup. Foula, on the other hand, is pronounced 'foola' not 'fowla', although he makes a fair attempt at Muckle Flugga.
